case_note.introduction: This case involves two linked accounts in the same holder's portfolio that received small deposits totaling $4,426.44 from two external parties and dispersed $731,906.52 to two payees across 11 transactions in September 2022, all in Chinese Yuan. The alerts were driven primarily by SHAP attributions that flagged the internal transfer between accounts as high-risk due to perceived use of multiple currencies, transaction rate, and ACH format, but the actual transaction data shows all activity in a single currency (Yuan) and does not reveal the multi-currency pattern the model attributed.
case_note.body: Account 18196:80B1BF360 received $1,528.88 via cheque from counterparty 19740:808F65F10 on 2022-09-08 (T4094970), received another $1,528.88 from the same counterparty on 2022-09-09 (T4465300), and received $1,368.67 total from a second external payer (112078:809F5A2A0) via two transactions on 2022-09-09 (T4572097, T4572098). On 2022-09-08 at 19:35, account 18196:80B1BF360 transferred $3,617.11 via ACH to linked account 30416:80B1BF2C0 (T4134189). Between 2022-09-08 20:23 and 2022-09-09 15:24, account 18196:80B1BF360 initiated seven outgoing payments totaling $731,906.52 to two payees: counterparty 34828:80EF9A260 received $729,117.94 across four transactions (T4144011, T4144010, T4638636, T4638637), and counterparty 232304:80BC38F60 received $2,788.57 across two transactions (T4331476, T4331475). Account 30416:80B1BF2C0 received the $3,617.11 transfer and initiated no further outgoing activity. All transactions occurred in Yuan with no currency conversion evident in the transaction records.
case_note.conclusion: Pull the complete transaction history and account opening records for both accounts and their external counterparties, particularly 34828:80EF9A260, which was the destination of 99.7% of outgoing value. Obtain the stated business purpose and any commercial documentation (invoices, contracts, shipping records) supporting the large round-amount payments to 34828:80EF9A260. Clarify whether the inbound deposits represent collection from customers on behalf of a legitimate business purpose and whether the concentrated outbound transfers represent settlement, commission payment, or vendor payment consistent with that purpose. The SHAP attribution's reference to five distinct currencies contradicts the transaction data, which shows Yuan-only activity; investigate whether this discrepancy reflects data not shown in the sample or a model training artifact. The case cannot be closed without understanding the origination and purpose of the inbound funds and the commercial basis, if any, for the immediate onward dispersal to a single concentrated payee.

case_note.introduction: This case involves 11 accounts exhibiting high-volume internal transfers and heavy receipt of funds from external parties, concentrated in Saudi Riyal. The case shows characteristics of a gather-scatter layering topology: funds flowing in from 23 external sources ($167.8k) are internally redistributed across the group, then dispersed outward to 9 external payees ($57.1k). The pattern is marked by dense interconnection among member accounts, rapid sequential transfers, and significant embeddedness scores flagged by the model, all consistent with money laundering through account-to-account layering.
case_note.body: On 2022-09-08 to 2022-09-10, external party 70:100428A08 sent multiple deposits into the case (T4078617, T4157040, T4157041 totaling $15.7k), while party 223:811B8EE20 made smaller deposits (T4147110, T4483366). These inflows and others from 21 external parties were immediately recycled through the case membership as internal ACH transfers. Notably, account 222:811B83280 received multiple deposits from party 70:100428A08 and rapidly redistributed funds internally: T4215001 ($14.2k to 222:811B83280 at 23:38 on 9/8), T4215002 ($14.1k to 222:811B83280 at 11:46 on 9/9), T4656378 ($7.6k from 222:811B83280 on 9/10). Similarly, 48309:811C599A0 received concentrated inflows (T3123487, T3732500, T4656377, T2244742 totaling $62k) and moved funds outward, while 150240:812D22980 received T2244741 ($10.1k) and dispersed T4829454 ($394.60) and other transfers. The internal network shows no pass-through structure; instead, multiple accounts act as partial hubs. Account 119:81235E8B0 collected from five payers (T4269461 sourced $13k outbound), and 148016:811C597B0 received from four sources with minimal onward activity. The timing is clustered and rapid—most transactions fall within a 48-hour window (9/8–9/10), and account 119:811C597B0 contains a self-transfer of $3.77M (T3240081) on 9/10, the largest single movement observed.
case_note.conclusion: This case should be escalated for L2 investigation of the external parties 70:100428A08 and 223:811B8EE20, which appear to be primary funding sources, and the primary distribution hubs 222:811B83280 and 48309:811C599A0. Pull full transaction histories for all 11 accounts beyond the sample shown, account holder KYC records, and stated business purpose documentation. Resolve whether the accounts are related beneficially or represent a mule network, and identify the ultimate origin of the $3.77M self-transfer on T3240081 and its destination. The evidence sample shows only 40 transactions against a 116-transaction total; determine whether the unseen 78 transactions continue the gather-scatter pattern or establish a different structure. External party 70:100428A08 is flagged as a high-degree hub dealing with 564 parties across 1,787 transactions; cross-reference for other spoke cases and determine the legitimacy of that external entity's business model.

case_note.introduction: This case involves two accounts that received multiple inbound transfers in Yuan (primarily via credit card from a single external counterparty) over a five-day window in September 2022, then moved funds onward via ACH in mixed currencies. Account 19318:8106B1750 is the primary hub, receiving $13,524.23 from two external parties and dispersing $6,585.91 to two external payees, including an internal transfer to account 11904:803197B30. The case shows characteristics of potential layering activity — rapid conversion between currencies and payment formats — but the account volumes are modest and the transfers lack clear laundering topology.
case_note.body: Account 19318:8106B1750 received five inbound transactions between September 8 and 10, 2022. Three identical credit card deposits of $3,722.06 each (T4095084, T4412029, T4903322) arrived from counterparty 12278:804A100F0 in Yuan; a cheque deposit of $1,328.11 (T4505853) and wire transfer of $1,029.95 (T4505854) came from counterparty 35303:80F9F3E80, also in Yuan. On September 9 at 10:54 AM, the account executed a self-transfer of $1,386.96 (T1191352) converting Yuan to US Dollar, and simultaneously transferred $1,428.16 via ACH to account 11904:803197B30 (T1191353). Account 11904:803197B30 received only the single ACH transfer (T1191353) and initiated no outbound activity. Later on September 9, account 19318:8106B1750 sent $5,157.75 via ACH to external counterparty 18196:807FDA6D0 (T1191354), with the funds remaining in Yuan. The sequence shows currency conversion and use of multiple payment formats (credit card, cheque, wire, ACH) within a compact timeframe.
case_note.conclusion: Pull the full transaction history for both accounts 19318:8106B1750 and 11904:803197B30 beyond this five-day window to establish baseline activity and determine whether rapid multi-format transfers are routine. Obtain KYC documentation and stated business purpose for both accounts, particularly to explain the repetitive identical deposits from 12278:804A100F0 and the mixed-currency outbound movement. Verify the identities and business relationship of external counterparties 12278:804A100F0, 35303:80F9F3E80, and 18196:807FDA6D0. The evidence here is limited to a sample window; if this represents a small portion of a larger transaction set, the fuller picture may reveal layering or placement activity not visible in this snapshot. The modest dollar amounts and lack of a clear multi-hop intermediary chain weigh against immediate assessment, but the currency conversions, format diversity, and rapid throughput in a narrow time window warrant deeper investigation.

case_note.introduction: This case involves 72 accounts that form a dispersal network distributing funds across thousands of external counterparties. The model flagged the accounts based on small, rapid transfers in multiple currencies using ACH and check formats, with activity showing burst patterns and high layering-stage characteristics. No recognized laundering topology is evident in the sample shown, but the case structure—$61.2M inbound from 975 external parties flowing to $13.8B outbound to 17,675 external parties—resembles a possible integration or service-provision hub rather than a traditional money laundering ring.
case_note.body: The 40 transactions shown span September 8–10, 2022, and display uniform characteristics: predominantly small amounts ($159–$21,855), rapid sequential timing within single days, multiple currency pairs (EUR, USD, CNY, INR), and use of ACH, checks, and credit cards with no currency conversion. The accounts appear to receive funds from multiple external payers and then distribute them outward. For example, account 23691:8021353D0 received inbound transfers and shortly after dispersed funds via T3838864, T4635780, T4756602, T3857993, and T5003717 to counterparties across several currencies. Accounts 15231:80266F880 and 10344:808D193A0 show similar patterns: rapid collection followed by dispersal. Account 16643:80296BAF0 received $13.6M inbound across 43 transactions with zero outbound activity in the sample, consistent with an endpoint collection account. The wide external reach (two accounts each with 10,902 and 6,722 payees outbound) and the presence of 15 hub counterparties dealing with 13–54 distinct parties each suggest this case is one spoke in a larger structure not fully visible in the alert sample.
case_note.conclusion: Escalate to L2 investigation. Pull complete transaction history for the two highest-volume dispersal accounts (70:100428660 and 70:1004286A8) and the large collection account (16643:80296BAF0) to determine whether funds are flowing through for legitimate payroll, vendor payments, or financial services, or whether they are being layered through legitimate-appearing dispersal. Obtain KYC and stated business purpose for the 72 accounts and for the 15 hub counterparties identified externally. Cross-check whether the inbound $61M and outbound $13.8B are proportionate, whether the currency pairs align with any declared business, and whether the external counterparties form coherent customer or vendor bases. The sample shown cannot rule out integration-stage activity, and the case scale and external reach warrant deeper review before any closure determination can be made.

case_note.introduction: Two accounts linked by six internal ACH transfers of Saudi Riyal within a 36-hour window on 2022-09-09 to 2022-09-10. Account 119:812A09CF0 received five deposits totaling $47,681.04, and account 49365:812A09D40 received three deposits totaling $9,952.00, with funds flowing between them in a pattern where one account receives and rapidly forwards to the other. The model scored both accounts at 1.0, citing ACH payment format, transaction volume, and high layering-stage activity share as risk drivers. A potential CYCLE or GATHER-SCATTER topology is suggested by the tight temporal clustering and bidirectional movement.
case_note.body: The activity begins on 2022-09-09 at 05:39 UTC when account 119:812A09CF0 receives $14,881.67 (T4389486). Over the next 8 hours, three more deposits arrive at 119:812A09CF0: $13,702.37 (T2830849), $4,524.58 (T3712859), and receipts from external source 119:811EFA110 totaling $1,741.88 in credit card and cheque formats (T4696398, T4696397). At 09:36 UTC the same day, account 49365:812A09D40 receives $8,210.11 from 119:812A09CF0 (T2277134), which it then forwards outward. The pattern continues: 119:812A09CF0 receives $3,377.86 on 2022-09-10 at 08:12 UTC (T4010245) and $11,194.57 at 22:42 UTC (T5070515). All internal transfers are ACH format and same-currency (Saudi Riyal). Account 119:812A09CF0 acts as the primary collector with five inbound internal transfers, while 49365:812A09D40 receives three deposits but distributes five outbound transactions. The total value flowing through 119:812A09CF0 inbound is $47,681.04 against $8,210.11 outbound to the case; 49365:812A09D40 shows $9,952.00 inbound against $47,681.04 outbound, indicating funds collected by 119:812A09CF0 are being funneled through 49365:812A09D40 to external destinations not visible in this case.
case_note.conclusion: Escalate to L2 for investigation of the external destination(s) receiving the $47,681.04 forwarded by 49365:812A09D40 and the nature of the relationship between these two accounts. Pull full account KYC files, customer-stated business purpose, and transaction history outside the flagged window to establish whether this represents legitimate wholesale or remittance processing or whether it is consistent with a layering pattern. Determine the identity and business relationship of external source 119:811EFA110 and whether the small initial deposits ($1,741.88 via credit card and cheque) seed a larger structured movement. The tight clustering, rapid transit between accounts, and high proportion of layering-stage activity warrant second-layer review. This case may represent a spoke of a larger network if other case members exist outside this alert cluster.

case_note.introduction: This case involves four accounts that received modest inbound funds from seven external parties totaling $185,766 over two days in September 2022, then rapidly dispersed $1.65M outward to two external parties. The activity shows characteristics of a gather-scatter pattern: many small-to-medium deposits collected, then nearly all funds moved out to a narrow set of destinations within hours. The model flagged the two highest-scoring accounts due to the use of ACH as payment format, multi-currency conversion activity, and unusual velocity and concentration patterns.
case_note.body: Account 214615:8075AC7C0 (highest score 0.9999) received $1,769.52 in deposits and sent out $1,621,464.68, including two large transfers to external payee 111425:8093599E0 totaling $787,575.49 via ACH and cheque on 2022-09-09 (T4579661, T4579660), with duplicate transfers the following day (T5034913, T5034914). Account 218502:80705A7B0 (score 0.9999) received $25,138.27 in three deposits and made no outbound transfers; it was the recipient of a $21,594.47 transfer from 214615:8075AC7C0 on 2022-09-08 in Ruble via ACH (T1237957). Account 21918:810E74260 (score 0.8644) received $13,481.08 from three payers including $12,580.18 from 214615:8075AC7C0 in Euro on 2022-09-08 (T1237953) and made no outbound transfers. Account 136334:80D71C940 received $191,690.95 from three external payers and sent $72,923.95 to one external payee 135034:80DB056B0 in three Brazil Real transactions on 2022-09-09 (T4641701, T4641700, T4641699). The inbound flows from external parties 235509:80CE154B0 and 220:8026D8240 and others are small and fragmented across payment formats (wire, cheque, cash, credit card, ACH) arriving over the 2-3 day window, while the outbound consolidation through 214615:8075AC7C0 is concentrated and large, suggesting a collection and redistribution function.
case_note.conclusion: Escalate for L2 review of the fund origination and destination. Pull the complete transaction history and KYC files for accounts 111425:8093599E0 (the primary outbound recipient of $787k+) and 235509:80CE154B0 (the largest single inbound source at $177k in Brazil Real). Obtain wire instructions, beneficiary confirmations, and business rationale for the multi-currency conversions and the apparent duplicative transfers between 2022-09-09 and 2022-09-10. Determine whether the fragmented inbound deposits represent legitimate collections (e.g., payroll aggregation, customer receivables) or structured placement, and whether the rapid outbound concentration is consistent with a stated business purpose. The case structure is consistent with layering via account proliferation and currency conversion, but the absence of KYC context prevents a definitive assessment of whether these accounts operate as pass-throughs in a larger network or serve a legitimate aggregation function.

case_note.body: Account 123612:808D898B0 received four inbound transfers: £4,455.12 via cheque from counterparty 5:807EEA350 on 2022-09-09 (T4627089), and three ACH transfers on 2022-09-10 totalling £12,832.48 from counterparties 220572:808D894F0 (£4,138.92 and £4,183.64 via T4932852 and T5065674) and 20486:808D89540 (£4,309.92 via T4932853). Account 22155:808D89450 received three inbound ACH transfers on 2022-09-10 totalling £12,432.48 from the same external counterparties (220572:808D894F0 contributed £4,138.92 via T4932852, and 20486:808D89540 contributed £4,309.92 via T4932853), plus received the £1,862.83 transfer from 123612:808D898B0 (T5065673). The total inbound value to the case (£19,911.06) has not been withdrawn to external parties; instead it has been shuffled between the two accounts and remains resident.
case_note.conclusion: Escalate for investigation of both accounts' KYC files, stated business purposes, and relationship to the three external payers. Obtain documentation explaining the source of the five inbound transfers and the business rationale for the internal redistribution. The absence of outbound movement to third parties and the small number of accounts (two) means no definitive topology can be confirmed from this window alone; an investigator must determine whether this represents the middle of a larger network or self-contained funnel behavior.

case_note.introduction: This case involves five accounts engaged in a high-velocity internal transfer pattern concentrated over two days (September 8–10, 2022), with one account (70:100428810) dispersing approximately $1.4 billion to over 1,000 external payees. The group exhibits characteristics consistent with a gather-scatter topology: small inbound receipts consolidate into a hub account, which then redistributes outward at massive scale. The concentration of activity in odd hours (late night and early morning) and the circular motion of funds between a small number of internal accounts raise concerns about potential layering activity, though the evidence shown represents only 0.1% of the hub account's total transaction volume.
case_note.body: Account 70:100428810 is the transaction hub, receiving $16,420.10 from 56 payers across the visible transactions and dispersing $1,397,208,280.04 to 1,061 distinct external payees. Between September 8–10, this account transferred small amounts internally to four receiving accounts within the case: T4106189 ($352.27 cheque to 7:808D836C0), T4106190 ($1,079.82 credit card to 7:808D836C0), T4155009 ($1,982.77 cash to 222773:808C07DC0), and T4155008 ($3,876.44 cheque to 222773:808C07DC0). Account 212:80843D3E0 received three identical transfers of $11,829.08 each from the hub—T4174162, T4280156, and T4891570—all via cheque on the morning and overnight of September 8–9. Account 23731:81204C270 received two internal transfers from the hub totalling $318.26 (T4307119 and T4307120), then on September 9 returned $279.66 back to 70:100428810 via credit card (T4945019). Accounts 7:808D836C0 and 222773:808C07DC0 each received multiple transfers from the hub and made no outbound payments; they accumulated $16,226.00 and $14,570.80 respectively. The circular motion between 70:100428810 and 23731:81204C270—where funds move in and then return within hours—combined with the repetitive identical transfers to 212:80843D3E0 and the concentration in odd hours (02:30–04:21 GMT), suggests possible rapid churning to create layering rather than legitimate inter-account operations.
case_note.conclusion: Pull the complete transaction history for all five accounts, focusing on the 3,509 transactions not shown here. Obtain account opening documentation, beneficial ownership records, and stated business purpose for 70:100428810 and each receiving account. Identify the 56 upstream payers feeding the hub and investigate whether they are connected entities or genuinely independent sources. Cross-reference the 1,061 external payees against known money mule networks and high-risk jurisdictions. Determine whether the circular transfers between 70:100428810 and 23731:81204C270 are part of a legitimate accounting practice or evidence of round-tripping. The sample shown accounts for less than 0.1% of account 70:100428810's activity, so the true pattern may be far larger or entirely different from what is visible here. Until the full dataset is reviewed and the account purposes are established, the hub activity cannot be ruled benign.

case_note.introduction: This case presents a classic funnel-account topology: account 213580:80993EAE0 received 32 ACH deposits totaling $64,707.90 from 32 distinct external counterparties between 09-09 and 09-10, followed immediately by a single $4,764.20 transfer outbound to account 12719:80992E270 within this case. The structure matches the FAN-IN pattern and FinCEN's definition of a funnel account—rapid collection of many small inbound deposits followed by rapid onward movement. The model scored both accounts at 0.9864 based on ACH format, multiple currencies, and the internal transfer amount.
case_note.body: Between 09-09 at 08:31 and 09-10 at 18:57, account 213580:80993EAE0 received 32 consecutive ACH deposits in US dollars from 32 separate counterparty accounts. These deposits ranged from $297.54 (T5034941) to $4,782.59 (T5034950), with a median around $1,500. Notable larger deposits include T5034950 ($4,782.59), T5034962 ($2,345.89), T5034946 ($3,483.65), T5034956 ($3,563.06), T5034943 ($2,528.14), T5034945 ($2,543.80), and T5034966 ($3,756.27). The timing is highly compressed: 32 deposits in less than 37 hours, with a cluster of 18 transactions in a seven-minute window on 09-10 between 18:48 and 18:54. On 09-10 at 18:36, immediately after this inflow was well underway, account 213580:80993EAE0 forwarded $4,764.20 via ACH to account 12719:80992E270 (T5034964). Account 12719:80992E270 received only this single inbound transfer and made no onward transfers within the case window. All transactions are USD-denominated ACH transfers with no cross-currency element. The SHAP attributions cite currency flags and sender metrics that do not align with what the transactions show; the actual risk driver is the topology itself—many distinct payers to one collector with rapid onward dispersal.
case_note.conclusion: Escalate for L2 investigation. Pull the KYC and account-opening documentation for both 213580:80993EAE0 and 12719:80992E270 to establish stated business purpose and identify the beneficial owner(s). Obtain transaction history for both accounts for the preceding 6-12 months to assess whether this pattern is habitual or isolated. The 32 external counterparties should be reviewed to determine whether they are affiliated entities, payroll accounts, vendor payments, or genuinely independent parties—their account scores are all at or near 0.0, suggesting they were not flagged individually. Establish whether account 12719:80992E270 represents the final destination or whether the $4,764.20 was subsequently moved out via channels not captured in this evidence window. The case shows a completed funnel shape with compressed timing and does not contain evidence of legitimate business purpose; absence of KYC context prevents definitive characterization of the counterparties' relationship to the receiving entity.

Separately, on 2022-09-10 at 17:48:00, account 112637:8053704E0 passed through a $3,176.96 ACH transfer to 13154:805370580 (T5028871), which then moved no further. The visible sample of 39 transactions shows account 70:100428780 making outbound payments in 26 distinct formats to 27 different counterparties, with amounts ranging from $1.91 to $10,115.72. All payments are Rupee-denominated. Account 14757:8059186D0 received funds from only two payers and redistributed nothing. Account 112637:805CACDE0 received inbound transfers and made one small outbound payment. The case structure shows 3,653 additional transactions (not shown) across 1,151 further counterparties with the highest individual model score of 0.0, suggesting the bulk of the outbound activity is to low-risk recipients or follows patterns the model does not flag.
case_note.conclusion: Escalate to L2 for examination of the complete transaction history for accounts 70:100428780, 14757:8059186D0, and 112637:805CACDE0. Pull all 3,653 unseen outbound transactions and their receiving counterparties to determine whether the dispersal follows a legitimate business pattern (such as payroll, vendor disbursement, or settlement distribution) or exhibits random scatter. Request the account opening documentation and stated business purpose for the hub account and its source accounts. Investigate whether the internal transfers between accounts are clearing-related or represent deliberate layering. The presence of multiple hub counterparties in the external network (16:80007F290, 12:8047A8E50, 71:8049D90D0, and others, each dealing with 10–12 distinct parties) suggests this case may be one spoke of a larger structure; cross-reference those hubs with other open cases. The SHAP attributions correctly identify the gather-scatter risk in account 70:100428780's network centrality, but the disposition depends on whether the 3,653 additional outbound transactions reveal a pattern consistent with legitimate high-volume payment processing or show characteristics of mule-network dispersal.

Account 118:80F03EC20 received two transfers from account 70 on September 9: $3,263.31 via cheque (T4841832) and $709.76 via credit card (T4841833). Account 118 then made only eight outbound transactions totaling $16,533.22 to external parties. The hub's visible outbound payments shown here are small—cheques, credit cards, and cash ranging from $50 to $45,000—sent to dozens of distinct counterparties at high frequency (multiple payments per hour), with many amounts appearing in round figures or repeated values (e.g., $13,352.91 appears four times to the same counterparty 238190:80E4605F0).
case_note.conclusion: Escalate for L2 review. Pull the complete transaction records for account 70:100428978, particularly the 4,398 unseen transactions, to map the full payer composition and payee distribution. Obtain account-opening documentation and stated business purpose for all four accounts, with specific focus on account 70. Determine whether the inbound payers (the 75 external sources) share any common characteristics, ownership, or jurisdiction. Investigate whether the outbound payees (1,345+ distinct recipients) cluster by geography, business type, or relationship to the payers. The structure and scale strongly suggest layering activity: a small, dispersed inflow reconsolidated into a hub and then redistributed at scale to hundreds of destinations.
